_note: Figures transcribed from CGSI's own published research note, which is the SOURCE DOCUMENT behind CGSI_52_verified.csv. Nothing here is derived or estimated — every value is read off a numbered figure in the note, and the figure is cited per block. The note lives in the team hand-off pack (`D/ESG 52 Comapnies Data.pdf`), which is git-ignored, so the numbers are transcribed into this file rather than parsed at runtime.

source.title: ASEAN Strategy — ESG momentum as an Alpha selection tool

universe_definition.text: Of the c.140 MSCI AC ASEAN Index constituents at the start of 2020 and c.110 by end-2024, 52 companies remained in the index throughout AND registered positive ESG score compound annual growth over 2019-2023.
universe_definition.correction: The index is the SELECTION UNIVERSE, not only the benchmark. Our own earlier reconstruction treated MSCI ASEAN as the benchmark alone and rebuilt the names from public ESG evidence; CGSI drew them from the index membership itself.

caveat_2025.text: As of YTD-28 Aug 2025 the ESG momentum basket UNDERPERFORMED the MSCI AC ASEAN Index by -4.6%, largely due to its ~45% weighting in the banking sector, which has lagged amid interest rate cuts tied to growth concerns. CGSI state that further analysis is required to isolate the precise drivers.
caveat_2025.why_it_travels: The headline 55.1% vs 6.4% is a 2021-2025 cumulative figure and is the number every deck reaches for. Showing it without this line presents a strategy as uniformly winning when its own author reports it lagging in the most recent period. A tool whose entire argument is that inconvenient evidence should be surfaced cannot omit its own.

single_stock_caveat.text: ESG improvements alone do not guarantee stronger share price performance at the single-stock level; the outperformance is a basket property.

filters: inclusion in CGSI's own coverage universe
high_conviction_17.how_to_read_our_agreement: Only the FIRST filter is an ESG signal. The second is sell-side coverage and the third is a buy recommendation — our engine has no view on either, and by HARD RULE 4 never issues a recommendation at all. So the blind-17 overlap measures agreement on one of three criteria, two of which we cannot see by construction. Report it as such: it is not a 70% disagreement about ESG.

esg_rating_column.figure: Figure 5 — 'Malaysian market exhibits the strongest score momentum'
esg_rating_column.header_verbatim: Reuters Code | Bloomberg Code | Company Name | Industry | ESG Rating | ESG Score | 5Y CAGR ESG Growth
esg_rating_column.finding: CGSI's own column is headed 'ESG Rating' and carries BB / BBB / B. It is NOT attributed to LSEG anywhere in that figure. The same document prints LSEG's own grades in its per-company briefs as an 'LSEG ESG Combined Score' on the A+..D- scale (A, A-, B+, B, B-, C observed). Two different scales, and only the second is attributed to LSEG.
esg_rating_column.consequence: `CGSI_52_verified.csv` renames this column to `lseg_rating`, which is an attribution CGSI did not make. We carry it as `incumbent_notch`, unattributed, and fetch the genuine LSEG score separately and live.

verification.method: All 52 rows of Figure 5 parsed from the note and compared field-by-field against CGSI_52_verified.csv.
verification.result: Zero mismatches across ESG Rating, ESG Score, 5Y CAGR and Industry for all 52 companies. The CSV is a faithful transcription of the note.
verification.delisting_marker: The note itself flags MAHB as MAHB.KL^B25 — Refinitiv's delisting convention — independently corroborating the CSV's delisted note.
